topSignals.title: MISO's FERC large-load tariff filing deadline is tomorrow (August 31) — no filing found yet as of this weekend check.
topSignals.text: MISO committed to file its Large Load Interconnection Reliability Requirements Tariff with FERC before end of August 2026, responding to the June 18 six-RTO show-cause order; a fuller response is due November 16. Neither MISO's own site nor trade coverage shows a filing yet — the first real test (flagged here August 28–29) of whether the reform converts into an actual tariff change lands within 24 hours of this digest. MISO Large Load Interconnection | Akin Gump

topSignals.title: Germany's EnEfG reform loosens the PUE bar for new data centers rather than tightening it — a detail not previously carried in this digest.
topSignals.text: Current law requires PUE ≤1.2 for data centers commissioned from July 1, 2026; the cabinet-adopted amendment (draft April 9, cabinet decision June 24) relaxes this to ≤1.3, and for existing centers raises the planned 2027/2030 ceilings from 1.5/1.3 to 1.6/1.4. Still pending Bundestag/Bundesrat passage this autumn — a proposal, not yet law — but worth flagging as background for any German SOFC-CHP siting case, since it slightly lowers the regulatory floor that on-site efficiency gains compete against. cloudmagazin | cms.law

topSignals.title: Priority-stack check: both Elcogen and Topsoe confirmed quiet over the weekend.

Topsoe's press room shows nothing beyond the August 27 H1 2026 financial disclosure already covered in this digest — no new SOFC/SOEC product, factory, or partnership news. items.text: Other players: No new stack/cell-level announcements from Bloom, FuelCell Energy, Ceres Power, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, Aisin, Sunfire, or Convion in the last 24–48h.
FERC six-RTO large-load reform: MISO tariff filing deadline tomorrow — see Top Signal #1.

Germany EnEfG: PUE relaxation detail — see Top Signal #2. Bundestag/Bundesrat passage still expected autumn 2026; the >23.6 GWh/>1 MW reporting-threshold question flagged August 28 remains unreconciled against the 500 kW installed-IT-power threshold from the June 24 cabinet draft.

Texas ERCOT audit: Unchanged — still targeting ~December 10, 2026 completion. Confirmed scope (queue ~474 GW, ~90% data centers; ~300 projects ≥75 MW in the Batch Zero audit; separate community-impact review for projects ≥25 MW) matches what's already on file; no new dated development.
Project Jupiter (NM): Supreme Court response due September 2 (see AI Data Center Deployments above).

Rolls-Royce SMR: Step 3 (Detailed Assessment) is still targeted for completion "in August 2026" per Rolls-Royce SMR's own published timeline. No Design Acceptance Confirmation/Statement of Design Acceptability found granted as of today — continuing to watch given the timing flagged August 27.

NuScale Power: No PPA signed as of today. The "could change everything" TVA-deal speculation flagged August 28 remains unconfirmed; commentary now points to a subsequent earnings call rather than an imminent signing.
Gas turbines, grid-scale batteries, PEM/hydrogen: no new dated developments beyond what is already on file.
Bloom Energy (BE): No trading session (Sunday). Nothing new since Friday's $228.11 close on the Mizuho/Clear Street upgrades already captured August 28.
FuelCell Energy (FCEL): No dated news today; Q3 2026 results call remains confirmed for September 2, 10:00 a.m. ET.
Ceres Power (CWR.L): No new announcement since the August 28 Total Voting Rights notice.

lcoe.text: Germany PUE relaxation (✎ indirect input, not a technical cost figure): a looser regulatory PUE ceiling (see Top Signal #2) marginally narrows the efficiency-driven case for behind-the-meter SOFC-CHP in Germany relative to standard grid-tied cooling/IT infrastructure, since the compliance floor is being lowered rather than raised. Directional only — no €/kWh or capex figure attached.

Gas price case (✓ unchanged, EIA STEO): confirmed unchanged — $3.44/MMBtu 2026 average, $3.03/MMBtu average for the remaining five months of 2026. Next STEO due mid-to-late September; no update expected before then.

Pending carry-forward: MISO tariff filing (due August 31), Germany EnEfG Bundestag/Bundesrat vote (autumn 2026), Texas ERCOT audit completion (~December 10, 2026), Project Jupiter NMED/State Engineer Supreme Court response (September 2), FCEL Q3 call (September 2), Bloom 10-Q (September 11), Ceres H1 2026 results (September, date unconfirmed), Bloom scandium class-action lead-plaintiff deadline (September 28), Rolls-Royce SMR GDA DAC (expected within weeks per the August 2026 target, not yet confirmed), Bloom Q3 2026 earnings (October 27).
